# Bank of Jinzhou Corp., Ltd. Notes to Financial Statements

December 31, 2009

(Unless otherwise specified, RMB Yuan is used as the unit of the amount of money)

## I. General Situations

Bank of Jinzhou Corp., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "the Bank" for short) is a limited corporation established through integral transformation of ownership of 15 Urban Credit Cooperatives including Lingyun Urban Credit Cooperatives in Jinzhou and Jinzhou City United Credit Cooperatives with approval of the People's Bank of China on the Written Reply to the Opening of Jinzhou Urban Cooperative Bank [Yin Fu (1997) No.29] in accordance with the spirit of the Notice Regarding the Establishment of Urban Cooperative Banks[Guo Fu (1995) No.25] issued by the State Council. The original name of the Bank is Jinzhou City Urban Cooperative Bank and was renamed as Jinzhou City Commercial Bank Co., Ltd on April 12, 2008 in the light of the document Notice of Some Problems on Changing the Name of Urban Cooperative Banks [Yin Fu (1998) No.94], jointly issued by the People's Bank of China and State Industrial and Commercial Administrations, and was renamed as Bank of Jinzhou Corp., Ltd on April 14, 2008, with approval of China Banking Regulatory Commission on the written Reply of China Banking Regulatory Commission about Renaming Jinzhou City Commercial Bank[Yin Jian Fu (2008) No.137].

The Business License Serial Number of the Bank is 210700004032898; the Finance License Code is B0127H2210001; the registered capital is 1.6534339 billion RMB Yuan; legal representative is Zhang Wei; and registered address is 69 Shifu Road, Taihe District, Jinzhou. By the end of reporting date, the biggest shareholder of the Bank was Jinzhou Financial Bureau with a shareholding proportion of 8.55%.

Approved by China Banking Regulatory Commission Liaoning Banking Regulatory Bureau[Liao Yin Jian Fu (2009) No.125], Bank of Jinzhou Shenyang Branch was set up on June 2, 2009, and formally went into operation on August 21, 2009.

Approved by China Banking Regulatory Commission Dalian Banking Regulatory Bureau[Da Yin Jian Fu (2009) No.318], Bank of Jinzhou Dalian Branch was set up on August 6, 2009, and formally went into operation on October 22, 2009.

Under the Bank, there are three branches, which include Tianjin Branch, Shenyang Branch, and Dalian Branch; there are 29 first-class sub-branches, among which there are 24 in Jinzhou, 2 in Fushun, 2 in Dandong and 1 in Tianjin.

The business scope of the Bank covers the following: absorbing public deposits, granting short, medium and long-term loans, handling domestic and international settlement, handling bill acceptance and discount, acting as an agent to issue financial bonds, acting as an agent for issuing, honoring and underwriting of government bonds, buying and selling government bond and financial bond, engaging in inter-bank lending, trading foreign exchanges for the Bank or on behalf of its customers, engaging in bank card business, providing letter of credit and financial guarantees, acting as an agent to handle collection and payment of money and issuance business as well, offering safe box service, and other businesses approved by China Banking Regulatory Commission.

The financial report was approved for declaration by the Board of Directors.

## II. Basis of preparation

The financial statements of the Bank was prepared with assumption of sustained operation, on the basis of transactions and matters which actually occurred, in accordance with Accounting Standard for Business Enterprises—Basic Criterion (decree of Ministry of Finance: No.33) issued by the Ministry of Finance on February

# 锦州银行 Annual Report 2009 年度报告

15, 2006 and Notice of the Ministry of Finance about Printing and Distributing<Accountant Criterion of Enterprise—Goods in Stock> and other 38 Explicit Rules (Cai Kuai[2006]No.3) and Notice of the Ministry of Finance about Printing and Distributing 38 Concrete Criterions Including <The Number 1 of Accounting Standard for Business Enterprises: —Guide of Applications> (Cai Kuai[2006]No.18) (hereinafter called as “New Accountant Criterion of Enterprise” for short) issued on October 30, 2006 and other related stipulations.

## III. Statement on Abiding by Accounting Standard for Business Enterprises

The financial report prepared by the Bank is in accordance with the requirement of Accounting Standard for Business Enterprises, which genuinely and integrally reflects the financial position, business performance, cash flow and other relevant information of the Bank.

## IV. Important Accounting Policies and Accounting Estimates

### (1) Important accounting policies

1. Accounting year

The Bank’s accounting year starts on January 1 and ends on December 31.

2. Recording currency

The recording currency of the Bank is RMB

#### 3. Accounting attributes utilized for accounting measurement

The Bank adopts the accrual basis of accounting. Historical cost is adopted in accounting. When the amount of the accounting elements conforms to the requirement of Accounting Standard for Business Enterprises and can be measured in a reliable way, replacement costs, net realizable value, present value, fair value can be used in measurement. As it is initially affirmed, financial assets and liabilities shall be measured in accordance with fair value. As the follow-up measurement is carried out, transaction financial assets and liabilities, and financial assets for sale shall be measured according to their fair value, and other financial assets and liabilities shall be measured at their historical cost or amortized cost.

#### 4. Foreign currency transactions and foreign currency translation

In respect of foreign currency business, transactions are recorded at separate accounts denominated in different foreign currencies at the date of the transactions and accounting report is prepared in RMB at the end of the reporting period. When preparing the statement of translation in RMB, the first step is to prepare respective statement denominated in different foreign currencies, then translate them into USD, and then translate USD into RMB, finally prepare the statement in RMB.

Foreign currency transaction is charged to account on the exchange rate at the date of the transactions. Remittance gains or losses derived from foreign currency business, and the translation of monetary assets and liabilities denominated in foreign currencies into standard money are calculated in respective accordance with exchange rate transacted on current day on the

balance sheet date; income and expense items dominated in foreign currency are translated on spot exchange rate at the date of the transactions, hence the translated earnings or losses herein shall be charge to profit statement.

For non-monetary items, translation difference of transaction financial assets is included in gains and losses of changes in fair value; translation difference that can be offered for sale and invested is included in changes in fair value reserves in financial assets available for sale in shareholders' equity.

#### 5. Cash and cash equivalents

Cash and cash equivalents refers to all cash in hand and call deposits in banks readily available for making payments, highly—liquid investments with a maturity of less than three months from the date of acquisition that are readily convertible to known amounts of cash and which are subject to an insignificant risk of change in value, including a sum of money deposited in the central bank (exclusive of legal reserve), due from banks and capital

lent, buying back the sale of capitals, etc.

#### 6. Financial assets

### (1) Classification and measurement of financial assets

The Bank classifies its financial assets into the following categories: trading assets; loans and receivables; held-to-maturity investments and available-for-sale financial assets according to the investment purpose and economic essence.

### ① Trading assets

A financial asset is classified as trading assets if it is acquired or incurred principally for the purpose of selling or repurchasing in the near term at fair value or if it is part of an identified portfolio of financial instruments that are managed together and for which there is evidence of a recent actual pattern of short-term profit-taking. With exception of derivative financial instruments served for hedge purpose, other derivative financial instruments are classified as trading assets.

Financial assets in this category are initially recognized at fair value and then measured at fair value. Trading cost is included in the income statement in the period in which they arise.

Gains and losses (exclusive of accrual interest) arising from changes in fair value of trading assets are included in the investment income and gains/(losses) of changes in fair value. The accrual interest is included into interest income.

##### ②Held-to-maturity investment

Held-to-maturity investments are non-derivative financial assets with fixed or determined payments and fixed maturities that the Bank’s management has the positive intention and ability to hold to maturity. Held-to-maturity investments are initially recognized at fair value plus transaction costs. This sort of financial asset shall be accounted on actual interest rate method and is measured based on amortized costs on the balance sheet date. When the Bank sells a certain held-to-maturity investment which is still not up to the maturity date within a certain accounting year and the amount of money of sales relative to this investment, is more than 5% (including 5%) of the total prior to selling, the remaining of this sort of investment should be reclassified into investment available for sale and this financial asset must not be classified as held-to-maturity investment again in this accounting year and within subsequent two complete fiscal years.

### ③ Loans and receivables

Loans and receivables are non-derivative financial assets with fixed or determinable payments that are not quoted in an active market, including customers' loans and investment in voucher-based national debt. This sort of financial asset shall be accounted on real interest method and carried at amortized cost less impairment allowances on each balance sheet date.

#### ④Available—for—sale financial assets

Available—for—sale financial assets usually refer to the financial assets which can not be classified as those measured at their fair value and its changes are counted into current profit and loss, held—to—maturity investment and loans and receivables. Available—for—sale financial assets are carried at fair value on the balance sheet date. Non—implemented gains arising due to the change of fair value should first be affirmed in the capital surplus for shareholders' equity before this financial asset is transferred or confirmed impaired in value, as it is actually transferred or identified to be impaired in value, then transfer the changes in accumulated fair value previously affirmed in shareholders' equity to the current gains and losses.

### (2) Terminated affirmation of financial assets

As the right of obtaining cash flow from financial assets has become due or been transferred and the Bank has already transferred almost all risks and remuneration related to ownership, the confirmation of this financial asset shall be terminated.

### (3) Determination of the fair value of financial assets

For financial assets existed in the active market, its fair value should be determined in accordance with quotations in the active market. The quoted price in an active market refers to the price which can be got from stock exchange, broker, trade associations, pricing service agents regularly, and it represents the actual market price in the fair transactions. For financial assets which do not exist in the active market, the Bank shall define its fair value using value-assessing technique. These value-assessing techniques include making reference to the price used by all parties who are familiar with situations and voluntarily conduct transactions in market trading, making reference to current fair value of other essentially identical financial assets and discounting method of cash flow and so on.

#### 7. Impairment of financial assets

### (1) Assets measured based on amortized costs

The Bank periodically performs evaluation to the objective evidence of whether or not individual financial asset or combination of financial assets exist decrease in value. As the objective evidence shows that financial assets produce value—decreasing due to one or multiple loss events after its initial affirmation and these loss events may produce influences that may reliably be estimated on this financial asset or the future predicted cash flow of this group of financial asset, the Bank shall make a decision that this item or this group of financial asset has be impaired and confirmed as impairment loss. The objective evidences of financial asset impairment which comprises the following loss events related to observable data that the Bank has already paid close attention to are as follows:

① Serious financial difficulties of the issuer or the debtor.

② The debtor’s breach of contract clauses, such as breach or overdue in payment of interest or principal;

③ Considering from economic, legal or other respects, the Bank makes a concession for financial difficulties of the debtor;

④ The debtor might close down or carry out other financial reorganization;

⑤ Because of significant financial difficulties of the issuer, this financial asset fails to continue to be traded on the active market;

⑥ Being unable to recognize whether or not the cash flow of a certain asset in a group of financial assets has already decreased, but it is found that the future predicted cash flow of this group of financial assets since its initial affirmation has indeed reduced and can be measured after making overall evaluation to it on the basis of public data.

⑦ Significant adverse changes in debtor's business in technique, market, economic or legal environment make equity instrument investors unable to recover the cost of investment.

⑧ The fair value of the equity instrument investment drops significantly or non-transiently.

⑨ Other objective evidences showing the impairment of the financial asset

The Bank shall first make individual evaluation to the objective evidences whether or not the financial assets with significant single amount have been impaired, subsequently conduct combined evaluation to the objective evidence whether or not the financial assets with non-significant single amount have been impaired. If the objective evidences show that the financial assets which are individually evaluated have not been impaired, the Bank shall conduct combined impairment evaluation by including it in the financial assets group with similar credit risk characteristics. The assets that are individually evaluated for impairment and have been affirmed or will continue to confirm the impairment loss shall no longer bring into the range of combined impairment withdrawal.

If objective evidence indicates that value—decreasing loss has taken place in loans and receivables or held—to—maturity investment, its value—reducing loss shall then be measured in accordance with the difference between accounting surplus of this asset and current value of predicted future cash flow (do not include future

credit loss that has not yet occurred ) calculated based on its real interest rate) .Value—reducing loss occurred will reduce accounting surplus of this asset by using allowance account, and the amount of impairment loss shall be charged to current gains and losses. If the contracted interest rate of loans or held-to-maturity investment is a floating one, then the discounted rate used for defining impairment loss is the present actual interest rate confirmed according to contract. In actual operating, the Bank may also determine the fair value by utilizing market value observed and make measurement to its impairment conditions on this basis.

For financial assets with mortgages, whether or not mortgages are executed, the current value of future cash flow should be estimated and calculated in accordance with the value of executed mortgages subtracting the amount of the cost of selling mortgages.

When making combined evaluation to the impairment conditions, the Bank shall group the financial assets according to similarity and correlativity of credit risk characteristics.

When making impairment combination evaluation and measurement to the future cash flow of a group of financial assets, the Bank shall take the contract cash flow of this group of financial assets and historical loss experience of the assets which have similar credit risk characteristics to this group of financial assets as basis. To reflect the actual conditions of this group of financial assets, the historical loss experience mentioned above shall be adjusted according to current data, including the reflection of actual conditions that do not exist during the period of historical loss and rejection of influences of those matters that do not exist at that time from the data of historical loss experience.

Estimations made on the changes in future cash flow of various assets combination should reflect the changes of relevant and observable data at various stages, which should keep uniform to the orientation of this change. To reduce the discrepancy between anticipated loss and the loss which actually occurred, the Bank shall periodically examine and approve the theory and assumption of estimated future cash flow.

When financial assets are unrecoverable, the Bank shall cancel them after verification and deduct corresponding impairment reserve of financial assets after completing all necessary procedures and defining amount of money of losses. The financial assets recovered after canceling shall deduct the current impairment loss of financial assets according to the amount recovered.

If the amount of subsequent impairment reserves decreases and this decrease is correlated with some event happened after affirming this impairment reserves (for instance, upgrading of borrowers' credit grade), the amount decreased should be returned by adjusting impairment reserve account. The amount returned shall be confirmed in current gains.

##### (2) Available—for—sale financial assets

As for available—for—sale financial assets, the Bank performs impairment assessment on them as individually significant financial assets. As the objective evidence shows that an impairment loss on available—for—sale financial assets has been incurred, the cumulative loss resulted from the decrease of fair value is removed from the shareholders' equity and recognized in the impairment assessment. The cumulative loss is the net amount after the initial cost of these available—for—sale financial assets deducting recovered principal and amortized amount, the fair value of impairment and impairment loss previously recognized in profit or loss.

For the available—for—sale debt instrument whose impairment loss has been confirmed, when fair value rises after the date and objectively relates to the event after the original impairment loss was recognized, the original impairment loss is reversed into the current gains and losses. For the available—for—sale equity instrument whose impairment loss has been confirmed, when fair value rises after the date and objectively relates to the event after the original impairment loss was recognized, the original impairment loss is reversed into shareholders' equity.

#### 8. Accounts of buying back the sale and sales with buyback

Buying back the sale means a contract that the Bank buys in relevant assets from its trading opponent at

a certain price according to stipulations in contract or agreement (including bonds, bills and loans), and then resells to the opposite side at the specified price at the date specified under contract. A sum of money for buying back the sale is to be charged to account according to actual payment as the relevant assets are bought in.

Sales with buyback refers to a contract that the Bank sells relevant assets (including bonds, sold bills) to its trading opponent at a certain price according to stipulations under contract or agreement, and then buys back from the opposite side at a specified price at the date specified under contract. Amount of sales with buyback is charged to account according to amount actually received as the relevant assets are sold out.

The bid-ask spread between buying back the sale and sales with buyback businesses shall be confirmed interest income or expenditure on the basis of actual method of interest rate during the buying back the sale and sales with buyback periods.

#### 9. Derivative financial instruments

Derivative financial instruments refer to derivative financial products established on the basis of basic products or basic underlying variables with its price being decided upon the change of later. Financial instruments include forward contract, futures contract, interchange and future right, as well as implements with one or more their characteristics. Initial measurement shall be confirmed on the basis of fair value on the day when the derivative trading contract is reached and be subsequently measured based on fair value. Value of assessment earnings or assessment deficit produced due to the changes in fair value are charged to current gains and losses, and simultaneously reflected in “derivative financial assets” or “derivative financial liabilities” items of the statement of assets and liabilities.

Some derivative financial instruments are embedded in non-derivative financial instruments (i.e. principal contract). The embedded derivative financial instruments and principal contract compose a hybrid instrument. If the hybrid instrument related with embedded derivative instruments has not been appointed as financial assets or liabilities which are measured based on fair value and their changes are charged to current gains and losses, and the following conditions are satisfied at the same time, this embedded derivative instruments should be split off the hybrid instrument and treated as individual measurement derivative instruments.

① No close relation with the principal contract exists in terms of economic futures and risks

② Having the same conditions as embedded derivative instruments. The instruments solely existed are also derivative financial instruments.

#### 10. Long-term equity investment

Long-term equity investment includes investment in equities that are under control or joint control of the Bank and significantly influenced by the Bank such investment in equities that are not under control or joint control of the Bank and significantly influenced by the Bank, also no quotation found in the active market, and their fair value cannot be measured reliably.

For such equity investment that has no joint control or major influence over the companies being invested and has no quotations in the active market, and fair value cannot be measured reliably, the Bank shall account on cost basis. Investment returns shall be affirmed as the companies being invested announce distribution profits or cash dividend on shares.

Long-term investment shall be charged to the balance statement on the basis of value after subtracting impairment reserve, and disposal or transfer of long-term equity investment shall be charged to current gains and losses in terms of difference between purchasing price actually acquired and value after subtracting impairment reserves.

#### 11. Fixed assets

Fixed assets refers to premises and buildings, mechanical equipment, electronic equipment, means of transport with a service life over one year that the Bank holds for operating purpose. Premises and buildings mainly include

network, properties and office buildings of branch offices. Fixed assets shall be measured based on historical costs and listed in terms of net value after original value deducting grand total depreciations and impairment reserve. Historical costs include the direct expenditure on the acquirement of fixed assets.

The later expenditure of fixed assets refers to costs of updating and repairing in the use process of the fixed assets. The guide lines of the later expenditure are: the assets meets the definition of fixed assets should be counted as a cost, while the carrying amount of the replaced part is derecognized. The assets does not meet the definition, should be counted in current profits and losses.

Fixed assets are depreciated by means of composite life method and withdrawn within the estimated service life according to their credit value minus estimated net residual value. For fixed assets whose impairment reserve has been withdrawn, the amount of depreciation can be confirmed according to the book value after deducting impairment reserve and the years available during future period.

<div style="text-align: center;">Estimated service life, rate of net residual value and annual rate of depreciation of fixed assets are listed as follows:</div>

As the economic interest cannot be produced due to fixed assets being disposed or anticipated utilization or disposal, the confirmation of fixed asset shall be terminated. The sum of incomes from sale, assignment, scrapping of or disposal for damage in fixed assets deducting the net book value and relevant taxes and fees shall be charged to current gains and losses.

As the recoverable amount of fixed assets is lower than its book value, the book value shall be written down to the recoverable amount.

## 12. Works in process

### (1) Pricing of works in process

Cost on works shall be defined according to expenses actually paid. Self-operating works should be measured based on direct material, labor and construction costs, contracted works shall be measured in accordance with purchase price of works payable, installation works of equipment shall determine cost on works according to the value of installed equipment, installation expense, and expenditure on trial run of the works. The cost of works also includes loan expense and exchange gain and loss that are in conformity with capitalized condition.

### (2) Standard and time point of works in process converted into fixed assets

The fixed assets built by the Bank, starting from the date of attaining scheduled serviceable condition, shall carry forward fixed assets based on estimated value in accordance with works budget, cost of building or actual cost of works, and start accrual of depreciation starting from next month. Adjustment shall then be made to the discrepancy of original value of the fixed assets after going through the formalities of final settlement of completed works.

## 13. Debt assets

Debt assets means physical assets or property right that the Bank is obtained from debtors, guarantors or a third person for compensation due to the performance of creditor’s right or security lien according to law.

Debt assets should be charged to account based on fair value from the date of obtaining them and the difference

# 锦州银行 Annual Report 2009 年度报告

between fair value and book value of relevant assets and tax fee paid shall be charged to current gains and losses. Assets for mortgaging debt shall not accrue depreciation or amortization.

Expenses occurred in the course of keeping assets for debt assets shall be directly charged to other operating cost, and expenses happened in the process of handling assets for debt assets shall be offset deduction from the disposal income.

In principle, it is not allowed to lease debt assets obtained. In case the debt assets that surely fail to be disposed within the specified time subject to objective conditions, can be leased temporarily within the disposal time limit under the condition that the establishment of lease relationship does not influence the disposal of assets. Rental income is charged to other operating income.

The disposed earnings of debt assets shall be charged to non-operating income as they are acquired, and disposal loss shall be charged to non-operating income.

## 14. Pricing and amortization method of intangible assets

### (1) Pricing method of intangible assets

Intangible assets include land use right, proprietary technology and non-proprietary technology and so on. Intangible assets brought in shall be used as actual costs in terms of the purchase price actually paid and other relevant expenditures.

For intangible assets invested by investors, actual costs should be defined according to the value stipulated in investment contract or agreement, but the actual costs should be determined in accordance with the fair value if the value stipulated in contract or agreement is not fair and equitable.

If the intangible assets obtained by the exchange of non-monetary assets are commercial in nature, they shall be charged to account according to the fair value of assets surrendered, or else, they shall be charged to account according to the book value of assets surrendered.

Intangible assets acquired through debt reorganizing shall be confirmed according to their fair value.

##### (2) Method and term of amortization of intangible assets

The land use right of the Bank shall be amortized on average according to the year limit of transfer from the date of transferring (acquiring the right of land use), proprietary technology non-proprietary technology and other intangible assets shall be amortized on average by installment in accordance with the shortest one among the three including estimated durable years, beneficial years specified in contract and valid years stipulated by law.

## 15. Long-term expenses to be apportioned

The long-term expenses to be apportioned mean various expenses with a apportion term more than one year (exclusive one year) that has occurred but should be born by current period and different periods later. Long-term repaid and deferred expenses shall be charged to account according to actual expenditure and amortized on average within the beneficial period of a project.

The long-term expenses to be apportioned of the Bank are mainly the expenses on decoration of premises leased for operating.

## 16. Impairment of non-financial assets

An impairment test must be made in case there is a hint of impairment of the fixed assets and other non-financial assets on the balance statement date. Where the impairment test result shows that the recoverable amount of assets is lower than its book value, an impairment reserve shall be withdrawn according to its balance and charged to the impairment loss. The recoverable amount of money is the higher between the net amount after the fair value of assets minus disposal expense and the current value of estimated future cash flow of assets. The impairment reserve of assets shall be calculated and affirmed on a single asset basis. If it is difficult to estimate the recoverable amount of the single asset, the recoverable amount of asset group shall be defined by the asset group to which

the asset belongs. Asset group is the smallest asset combination that can independently produce cash inflow.

After the impairment loss of relevant assets is confirmed, the Bank shall not be written back during later periods.

## 17. Financial liabilities

Financial liabilities are classified into two categories, financial liabilities measured at their fair value and their changes being charged to the current gains and losses, and that measured at their amortized cost.

### (1) Financial liabilities measured at their fair value and their changes being charged to current gains and losses.

Financial liabilities measured at their fair value and their changes being charged to the current gains and losses are divided into such financial liabilities held due to transaction and financial liabilities measured at their fair value and their changes being charged to current gains and losses that was appointed by management level when it made initial confirmation. Changes in all fair value should be charged to current gains and losses.

### (2) Deposits, bonds payable and other financial liabilities

Apart from being appointed as transaction-based bonds or financial liabilities being measured at their fair value and their changes being charged to current gains and losses, all bank savings, bonds payable and other financial liabilities shall be measured at their amortized costs.

Only when the current obligations of financial liability have wholly or partly been terminated, can the confirmation of this financial liability or a part of it be terminated.

## 18. Remuneration of employees

The remuneration of employees chiefly includes expenditures related to the acquirement of services provided by employees, such as wages, bonus, allowance and subsidy, welfare expenses for employees, social insurance premium and public accumulation fund of housing, trade union funds and educational fund of employees.

During the accounting period of employees providing services, the Bank defines the staff and workers' remuneration payable as liability and charges it to the costs and expenses of relevant assets according to the objects benefited from services provided by employees. Compensations given to employees due to terminating labor relationship with them shall be charged to current profit and losses.

The Bank takes part in the endowment insurance plan managed by the local government. Besides paying corresponding expenses for the endowment insurance, the Bank assumes other obligations for the retired staff. Insurance money shall generally be jointly undertaken by staff and the Bank. Expenses of insurance money assumed by the Bank shall be charged to current gains and losses as they occur.

In-service employees of the Bank shall all join the housing accumulation fund plan in accordance with stipulations of the local government. The Bank shall also pay housing accumulation fund for the housing public accumulation fund plan in a certain proportion of employees' wages, and charge them to current profit and losses as they occur.

## 19. Interest income and expenditure

Besides financial assets and liabilities being measured at their fair value and their changes being charged to current profit and losses, interest income and expenditures of other interest-bearing assets and liabilities shall be confirmed by means of effective interest method.

The effective interest method means a method calculating their amortized costs as well as interest income or interest expenses at various stages according to the effective interest of financial assets or liabilities (containing a group of financial assets or liabilities).

The effective interest refers to an interest rate that is used for discounting the future cash flow of financial assets or liabilities during anticipated survival period or during applicable shorter period into present book value of these financial assets or liabilities.

##### 锦州银行 Annual Report 2009 年度报告

While defining effective interest, the Bank shall estimate future cash flow on the basis of taking into consideration all contract clauses of financial assets or liabilities (including right of paying up a loan ahead of schedule, rising tendency options and similar options and so on), but without consideration of future credit loss.

Various charges, transaction expenses and premium price or reduced value etc. paid or imposed between parties signing a contract of financial assets or liabilities, and that attribute to the component of effective interest shall be taken into consideration while determining effective interest. When the future cash flow or survival period of financial assets or liabilities is unable to reliably estimated, it is necessary to adopt contract cash flow of these financial assets or liabilities within the entire contract period.

## 20. Fee and commission income

Fee and commission income shall usually be confirmed while offering relevant services.

Commission charges produced while engaging in bargaining of assets, or participating in the third party to conduct bargain transaction of assets (such as purchasing customers' loan, securities or selling them) shall be confirmed as the relevant transactions are accomplished.

## 21. Government subsidies

### (1) Conditions of recognition of government subsidies

Only under the condition of being able to satisfy the conditions appended to government subsidies and being capable of receiving government subsidies, can the governmental subsidies be recognized.

##### (2) Measurement of governmental subsidies

Where the governmental subsidies are monetary assets, they shall be measured in accordance with the amount received or receivable. Where the governmental subsidies are non-monetary assets, they shall be measured in accordance with their fair value, where their fair value cannot be reliably acquired; they shall be measured according to nominal amount of money (one Yuan).

The governmental subsidies relative to assets shall be recognized as deferred income and distributed on average within the time limit of service life of relevant assets and charged to the current gains and losses. However, the governmental subsidies measured in accordance with nominal amount of money shall be directly charged to current profit and loss. The governmental subsidies relative to gains shall be disposed according to respective conditions: Those that are used for compensating for relevant expenses or losses of the Bank during later period shall be recognized as deferred income and charged to current gains and losses when confirming relevant expenses. Those that are used for compensating for the Bank's relevant expenses or losses shall be directly charged to current gains and losses.

The governmental subsidies that have been recognized need to return shall be treated differently: where there existing related deferred incomes, the book balance of related deferred income shall be deducted, and the excess part shall be charged to the current gains and losses, or else, they shall be directly charged to current gains and losses.

## 22. Income tax and deferred income tax assets and liabilities

The income tax is the total of current income tax and deferred income tax.

The current income tax is the amount of current income tax calculated in terms of current taxable amount of income. The taxable amount of income derives from making corresponding adjustment to current accounting profit before tax in accordance with relevant stipulations in tax law.

Deferred income tax assets and liabilities are confirmed according to the calculation of difference (temporary difference) between tax—figuring basis of assets and liabilities and its book value. For offsetting deficit and offsetting deduction of taxation whose taxable amount of income can be offset deduction in subsequent years in accordance with the stipulations in tax law, they may be considered temporary discrepancy to confirm corresponding deferred income tax assets. For those temporary differences formed from initial affirmation of assets produced in the

transaction of neither influencing accounting profit nor taxable amount of income (or may offset against deficit), no corresponding deferred income tax assets should be affirmed. For deferred income tax assets and deferred income tax liabilities at the statement of assets and liabilities day, they should be measured in accordance with and applicable rate of tax during the period of expectedly recovering this assets or paying off this liabilities.

The confirmation of deferred income tax assets is limited to the taxable amount of income that the Bank could possibly gain for offsetting against temporary difference, deficits that can be offset deduction and offsetting taxation.

Deferred income tax corresponding to the fair value of financial assets available for sale shall be charged to the shareholders' equity and then transferred into current gains and losses when relevant financial assets are sold.

## 23. Operating lease

The Bank regards the lease where the leaser retains the main risks and remuneration of leased assets as the operating lease. The operating lease of the Bank includes the operating places and devices that the parent bank and other branches have leased. A sum of money paid shall be charged to operating expenses by amortization by means of composite life method within the lease term.

When the lease agreement is terminated in advance, all penalty expenditure paid for leaser shall be charged to current gains and losses as the agreement is terminated.

## 24. Contingent liabilities and acceptance

The contingent liabilities refer to the potential obligations formed in the past transactions or matters and its existence must be proved through occurrence or none occurrence of the future undefined matters; or current obligations formed in the past transactions or matters. Performance of this obligation is not that economic interest may be caused to flow off businesses or the amount of money of this obligation cannot be reliably measured.

The contingent matters will be revealed only in the annotations of financial statement. Only when this matter probably causes economic interest to flow off and this amount of money can be reliably measured, this matter shall only be confirmed and withdrawn.

Acceptance means promise to pay made to the bills that the Bank had issued to the customers. The Bank held that most business of acceptance would be settled at the same time that customers made payment. Acceptance is to be accounted in the subjects outside financial statement, or to be revealed as contingent liabilities and promise.

## 25. Guarantee contract

The Bank shall draw up following guarantee contracts: letter of credit and letter of guarantee. These guarantee contracts shall allow the Bank to pay a sum of money to the holder of guarantee contract on behalf of the guaranteed party in case the guaranteed party fails to perform contract terms.

The guaranteed amount of money of guarantee contract shall be shown as a subject outside financial statement.

## 26. Estimated liabilities

Owing to the current obligations formed from pending action, reorganization and deficit contract, its performance will probably cause outflow of economic interest. As the amount of money of this obligation can be reliably measured, it is confirmed as estimated liabilities. For operating deficit in the future, no estimated liabilities shall be confirmed.

The estimated liabilities shall be initial measured in accordance with optimum estimate of expenditure necessary for executing relevant current obligations and in overall consideration of risks, uncertainty and time value of money and other factors related to contingent matters. When the influence of time value of money is significant, the optimum estimates shall be determined by discounting relevant future cash outflow.

## 27. Commission businesses

Acting as an agent or going in for other commission businesses, the Bank holds and manages assets for

#### 锦州银行 Annual Report 2009 年度报告

other institutions. This financial statement does not contain trusteeship assets and incomes derived from them that for them. The Bank, acting as a consignee, trustee and an agent, undertakes the obligation of keeping and makes promise to return to customers.

The Bank grants trust loans for third-party accommodators. As a middleman, the Bank grants loans to accommodator in accordance with the aspiration of the third party providing fund, and signs a contract with the third-party accommodator to agree on being responsible for managing and recovering loan by replacing the third party. The third-party accommodator shall decide by himself the requirements and clauses of entrusting loan, including purpose, amount of money, and interest rate of loan and arrangement of paying up a loan. The Bank shall impose commission charge of entrust loans and confirm it as income in terms of ratio during the period of providing services. The Bank does not undertake the risk of loss produced by a loan.

## 28. Other comprehensive income

Other comprehensive income refers to interest earned which is not recognized in gain and loss and the net amount which is including the deduction of income tax in accordance with the Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises

## 29. Segment reporting

The operation segment is divided in accordance with the internal organizational structure, Management requirements, Internal reporting systems, which is the basis of Reporting Segment.

The operating segment is divided into in accordance with the characteristics of the Bank’s business corporation banking, personal banking, fund business and other business. The transferred price between segments shall be priced by means of single funds pond pricing in accordance with the time limit of source and utilization of funds. The supplier and employer of funds shall be valued in terms of the same interest rate and the transferred price between segments of the Bank shall be worked out by referring to the currency market interest and quotation with higher degree of marketization on the basis of calculating actual fund cost in detail. Expenses shall be distributed between different segments in the light of beneficiary conditions.

The degrees of dependence on the main customers see Note.

### (2) An important accounting estimation and judgment

Based on historical experience and such factors as reasonable expectation to the future events, the Bank has made the following indefinite estimation and would continue to carry out follow-up evaluation. The main domains

of book value of assets and liabilities influenced by accounting estimation and hypothesis are listed as follows. It is unreal to define the influence brought by changes in the following important hypothesis or other estimations. The Bank will possibly make a major adjustment to these estimations in accordance with actual conditions in the days to come.

## 1. Loan asset impairment loss

Unless the known conditions indicated that value—decreasing loss have already taken place during the reporting period between the evaluations every time, the Bank will carry out periodical check to the book value of customers' loans and make judgment of whether or not there exists objective evidence showing that value—decreasing loss has occurred in customers' loans. If the objective evidence indicated that value—decreasing loss has occurred in customers' loan, the Bank will estimate the amount of value—decreasing loss. The amount of value—decreasing loss is the difference between the book value of customers' loan and current value of estimated future cash flow. In the course of estimating value—decreasing loss, it is necessary to make a great number of judgment to define whether or not there exists objective evidence showing occurrence of value—decreasing loss, and require to make a major estimation to the current value of estimated future cash flow so as to reduce the discrepancy between estimated value—decreasing loss of loan and actual value—decreasing loss of loan.

## 2. Impairment loss of other assets

The Bank makes impairment evaluation per year to other assets with exception of customers' loans to judge whether or not there exists a hint of decrease in estimated cash flow. The Bank also estimates the amount of decrease in cash flow and makes depreciation of impairment reserve to it.

## 3. Fair value of financial instruments

For financial instruments unable to obtain quotations of active market, the Bank confirmed their fair value using assessment technique. Technique of assessment contains present discounted value (PDV) of cash flow and so on. Technique of assessment should as much as possible use observable data in actual operation, but management level is still required to make estimation to such factors as credit risk of parties conducting transactions, fluctuation ratio of market and its relativity. If change in the hypothesis of the above factors takes place, evaluation to the fair value of financial means will be affected.

## 4. Held – to–maturity investment

The Bank regards non-derivative financial assets with a fixed or definable paid amount and a fixed maturity date as a held-to-maturity investment. This classification involves major judgment. When related judgment is made, the Bank will take into consideration that whether or not it has willingness or ability by itself to hold this sort of investment up to the date due. If the Bank is about to sell at more than 5% of the total prior to selling relative to this investment before the investment is at maturity date, the Bank must reclassify the remainders of this sort of held-to-maturity investment into financial assets available for sale and measure the corresponding investment at their fair value, instead of amortized costs.

## 5. Income tax

Within the limit of taxable amount of income tax probably acquired for offsetting against and being capable of offsetting against temporary difference, the Bank will confirm deferred income tax assets produced from temporary difference that is offsetting against deduction. At the statement of assets and liabilities day, the Bank will make recheck to the book value of deferred income tax assets. If it is likely to fail to obtain adequate taxable amount of income for offsetting against deferred income tax assets during future period, the book value of deferred income tax assets should be decreased. Therefore, the Bank needs to make major judgment to the tax disposal of relevant transactions in accordance with relative tax laws and regulations, and make major estimation to the possibility of whether or not being able to obtain enough taxable amount of income for offsetting against deferred income tax assets.

Note: according to Accountant Criterion of Enterprises, the Bank discounted the cash flow to test and calculated loan impairment reserve using migration model. The loan impairment reserve withdrawal means estimating and calculating the present cash flow value of loans so as to withdraw loan impairment reserve in accordance with the reimbursement ability, the reimbursement situation of loan principal and interest of borrower, the rational value of guarantee or pledge and actual guarantee ability of guarantor. The loan impairment reserve was withdrawn by means of single impairment test and combined depreciation test respectively. In the practice, the single loan

impairment test method was to conduct loan impairment test by virtue of the discount model of future cash flow, and withdraw the impairment reserve according to the result of estimation and calculation. In the combined impairment test, the Bank, by taking loans with similar characteristics as a whole using migration matrix model, withdrew the impairment reserve for loan combination on the basis of analysis of variation in loan classification and historical data lost. With respect to normal and special-mentioned loans, the ratio of loan migration to substandard and doubtful loans was regarded as the loan default rate, which multiplied by the default loss rate of substandard and doubtful loans, and the result was taken as the expected loss rate, on the basis of which, the combined impairment reserve was calculated. The impairment reserves for substandard and doubtful loans, of which the loans above the standard for single significant loans were withdrawn by means of single test, while those below the standard for single significant loans were withdrawn in accordance with the weighted mean proportion of single assessment withdrawal reserves respectively. The reserves of loss loans were withdrawn in the proportion of 100%.

In 2009, the Bank offered infrastructure loan of RMB 200 million Yuan to the shareholder of the Bank, Jinzhou Finance Bureau, which had not been recovered till December 31st, 2009.

The details are as follows: the total book value of the overlying bonds issued in December 2007 is 500 million RMB Yuan, with a bond term of 10 years (issuer's redeemable right was attached at the end of the fifth year). The nominal rate of the bonds in the first interest-bearing annuals would be unchanged and put into record by the bookkeeper, and in case the issuer fails to perform its redeemable right, the nominal rate within the last five interest-bearing annuals would, from the sixth interest-bearing annual to the maturity of the bonds, be 3 percentage points over that recorded by the bookkeeper. Simple interest instead of compound interest was adapted to the bonds on a yearly basis, and no overdue interest would be borne. The book value of each bond is 100 Yuan, and the debenture capital corresponding to each unit of account is 100 Yuan, (2) the nominal rate of the bonds in the first five interest-bearing annuals is 5.6%.

## 47. Segment reporting

The major businesses of the Bank are commercial loan and acceptance of deposits, and the existing personal and corporate loan funds mainly derived from customers' deposits.

The segment information is listed at the business segments of the Bank. The Bank provides such financial services depending on four major business segments: corporate banking business, personal banking business, treasury business and other business. The segment income, operating results, assets and capital expenditure listed in business segments include the items directly under various segments and related items distributable to various segments based on rational standards. As part of assets liability management, the sources and use of funds of the Bank are distributed to various business segments according to the natures of their businesses. The internal transfer price of funds shall be subject to the level of both benchmark interest rate and current market interest rate.

Corporate banking business — the Banking service provided for corporate customers, including home and foreign

#### 锦州银行 Annual Report 2009 年度报告

currency deposits, loans, products in connection with trade, as well as settlement, agency, commission, credit

authentication and other services.

Personal banking business — the Banking service provided for personal customers, including home and foreign currency deposits, investment deposit products, trusteeship, debit cards, credit, and the management, settlement, agency and credit authentication of personal assets and other services.

Treasury business —that including the management of interest rate, money market transaction, self-employment bond investment and assets management.

Other businesses— other business of the Bank means other segments that can not be independently listed and reported or the businesses that can not be assigned according to rational references.

## IX. Related parties and their transaction

#### (1) Related parties and related natural persons

When a party controls or exert great affect on the other or both parties jointly control or exert great affect on a third party, and both parties or more are simultaneously under control of or affected by a third party or more parties, the related party relationships are constituted. The term “control” means having the right to decide the financial and business policies of an enterprise. The term “jointly control” means to jointly control a certain economic activity as per agreement in the contract. The term “significant effect” means having the power to participate in decision-making of the financial and business policies of an enterprise, but having no power to control or jointly control together with any other party (parties) the formulation of these policies.

Principle for confirmation of related parties:

Where shareholders hold 5% or more of the Bank’s stocks and those hold 5% or above of the Bank’s stocks, which are jointly held by two or more shareholders, we call them the related parties of the Bank.

The Bank’s shareholding subsidiaries, jointly owned companies and affiliated companies constitute the related parties of the Bank.

Other enterprises that are controlled jointly controlled or can exert significant effect on the Bank’s business by the key management personnel of the Bank or their family members having a close relationship with them.

All the directors, supervisors, top management and key management personnel as well as their family members having a close relationship with them constitute the natural persons of the Bank.

## X. Other Important Issues

Till the end of reporting term, the paid—in capital of the Bank was RMB2,547,233,866.00, the registered capital in the business lisence was RMB1,653,433,800.00. The reason of the inconsistency was that the asset—addition and the capital—increase haven’t been registered.

## XI. Risk of Financial Instruments

### 1. Financial instruments

Financial instruments have been extensively used in the operating activities of the Bank. Using the fixed or floating interest rate, the Bank has taken in deposits of different terms and pumped these funds to the high quality assets so as to realize an interest rate spread higher than the average. To increase the interest rate spread, the Bank applied the short-term funds to the long-term loans with higher interest rate, besides, it maintained an adequate liquidity to ensure duly repayment of the mature debts.

### 2. Credit risk

The credit risk faced by the Bank refers to the risk of the counterparty or the defaulting of liability. When all the counterparties were concentrated in the same industry or territory, the credit risk would be bigger. The reason for it was that the different counterparties in the same territory would face the same development of economy, which could affect the ability of credit–repayment. The concentration of credit risk reflects the sensitivity of the Bank to some certain industry or location. As the main customer loan business is concentrated in Jinzhou city of Liaoning province, the Bank bears a concentrated credit risk, susceptible to the changes in the regional economy.

The Bank has established a whole set of estimation system for credit quality, which set the credit limit according to the risk level of the borrowers or the counterparties, and decided the collateral valuation or the assurance level. The relevant risk evaluation process included customer investigation, risk rating, approval of credit limit, credit examination and after-loan supervision, etc. The risk evaluation would be held regularly in order that the Bank could supervise the risk and take proper measures. In addition, the Bank used the same risk controlling procedure and policy on the assurance provided by the customer to reduce the risk. At the same time, the Bank would commonly obtain margins to reduce the credit risk.

### 3. Currency risk

In addition to a small portion of business in U.S. dollars, HK dollars and foreign currency, most of the Bank's businesses are conducted in RMB. The major principle for the Bank to control currency risk is to strive for an asset/liability match in each currency and to keep the currency risk within the limitation of the Bank. The management of the Bank has imposed limitation on the currency exposure and made routine monitoring.

### 4. Interest rate risks

The Bank’s interest rate risks mainly derive from the effect of market interest rate fluctuation on financial position and cash flow. The margin of the Bank, with the fluctuation of market interest rate, may increase or decrease, even make a loss due to unexpected fluctuation. For a long time, the prime rate for deposit and loan in China has been determined by People’s Bank of China. In general, the interest rates of interest-bearing assets and interest-payment liabilities change in the same direction. Therefore, in addition to foreign bond investment and part of off-balance sheet businesses, the Bank is faced with less interest rate risk. However, People’s Bank of China has never promised to maintain the present interest rate system.

The discount interest rate of bills is market-determined, but the lowest interest rate is regulated by People’s Bank of China.

The interest rate risks of the Bank are collected in the following table. The assets and liability items in the table are classified according to the earlier one between the date of re-offering and the maturity date, and listed according to their book value.

## 5. Liquidity risk

The Bank is facing various daily cash drawing requirements, including overnight deposits, current deposits, fixed deposits upon maturity, bonds payable, drawing of loans to customers, guarantees and other derivative financial instruments that are paid by cash, etc. According to experience in the past, quite a few matured deposits shall not be drawn out on the maturity date, but remain to be kept in the Bank instead, however, in order to cope with unforeseen demands for funds at the same time, the Bank defined the minimum limit to the amount of funds deposited, minimum amount of borrowed funds necessary to be kept and the amount of other funds borrowed to meet various cash drawing requirements.

In conformity to the requirement of Peoples’ Bank of China, the Bank limited the loan/deposit ratio to not more than 75%. Moreover, the general reserve and legal reserve, which are scheduled to hand up to People’s Bank of China, are unavailable for daily operating activities of the Bank. During the reporting period, People’s Bank of China adjusted the deposit proportion of deposit reserve many times.

### 锦州银行 Annual Report 2009 年度报告

## XII. Capital management

The target of the Bank’s capital management is to meet the demand of supervision, increase the ability of resisting risks, and promote the return of capital, and is to establish the target of the Bank’s capital adequacy rate on this basis, ensure the realization of management target by the means of plan examination and limit management to meet the demand of outside supervision, credit rating, risk compensation and shareholder return, and to promote the Bank’s risk management to guarantee the order of capital expansion, perfection of business structure and operational model.

The Bank’s business scale developed rapidly in recent years. The consumption of assets to capital expanded increasingly. In order to make the capital adequacy rate meet the supervision demand and provide biggest returns to shareholders under the premise of risk-control, the Bank established the concept of capital restriction, implemented capital management in terms of capital savings, gradually perfected the capital occupation mechanism, and established planed appraisal method which took the ROC as key measuring parameters. Meanwhile, the management of capital utilization was strengthened, operating capital was guided to increase concertedly by various management policies to decrease capital occupation and increase the ROC.

The Bank calculated and exposed the capital adequacy rate according to the Management Measures on Capital Adequacy Rate of Commercial Banks issued by CBRC and others relevant regulations.

Note: the reasons for the fluctuant of various financial targets are as follows:

Return of assets: the reason for ROA of 2009 higher than that of 2008 is the net margin and the profitability increased.

Core Capital adequacy ratio: the core capital adequacy ratio of 2009 was higher than that of 2008, the reason of which was that the asset—addition and the capital—increase reached 1,266,000,000 RMB, and the capital premium reached 1,266,000,000 RMB. The profitability increased obviously than that of last year.

Rate of Non-performing loans: firstly, the loan increased; secondly, macro-control policy was actively implemented, loan rhythm was kept, loan structure was optimized, the loan policy “three inspection” was carried strictly to effectively prevent the increase of non-performing loan; thirdly, monitoring and managing after loan was strengthened to realize risk monitoring, risk warning, risk discovering, accountability, and recovery of matured loan timely.

The credit concentration ratio of single group customer: firstly, the asset-addition and the capital-increase was 1,266 billion Yuan, and the capital premium was 1,266 billion Yuan; secondly, the uniform and centralized credit management to group customer and relevant customer was carried out, thirdly, loan structure was adjusted, the loans exceed standard were cleaned up, and the SMEs loans were expanded.

## 锦州银行 Annual Report 2009 年度报告

Provisioning coverage ratio: it increased substantially in 2009. The reason for it was the non-performing loan rate of the Bank was reduced and the level of risk compensation increased.

Migration ratio of doubtful loans: it increased for the reason that part of long-term overdue loans was reclassified into loss loans.

Bank of Jinzhou corp., Ltd.
